items.headline: Rayleigh mother was told to say her goodbyes before doctors found her daughter's type 1 diabetes
items.summary: Mandy hopes no other family goes through what hers did after Zara, then 13, was rushed to Southend Hospital with a life-threatening complication nobody had seen coming.
body: Zara had felt worn out on a family trip in August 2025. Back home she was sick and struggling to breathe, and at Southend Hospital she was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes and diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), a dangerous build-up that happens when the body runs short of insulin. Her mother says staff got a defibrillator ready in case her heart stopped, then told her to call the family in and prepare for the worst.

Looking back, the signs had crept up for months: stomach and back pains, tiredness, a thirst that never went away, frequent trips to the toilet and dizzy spells. Mandy says she had never heard of the 4Ts and still carries guilt for missing them, calling the ordeal "a catastrophic plane crash rather than a managed emergency landing". Zara spent a week in hospital and now lives like any other teenager, using a glucose monitor and an insulin pump.

Dr Deepa Shanmugasundaram, a GP and clinical lead at NHS Essex, said symptoms can develop quickly. Children who show them should be seen the same day through their GP or NHS 111, and anyone with those signs plus severe stomach pain, rapid breathing, vomiting or confusion needs 999 or A&E straight away. Mandy now runs a monthly meet-up in Rayleigh for families of children with type 1 diabetes.
points: The 4Ts of type 1 diabetes: toilet, thirsty, tired, thinner
Family meet-ups: second weekend of each month, 11.30am, Manzano Lounge, High Street, Rayleigh
Told for World Diabetes Day on Saturday 14 November
